address_range.note: One parcel spanning 123 and 125 Corbett Avenue.

hook: A 1937 Spanish Mediterranean house, built for $4,000 by the contractor Arthur Quinn with no architect.

historic_status.reason: No evaluation and 45 years or older

events.event: William Magner's grocery, saloon and basement meeting hall opened on this corner; it was the district's only hall until 1895, and the neighbourhood improvement clubs met in it.
Magner's store and hall burned to the ground, taking two neighbouring houses with it. The corner stayed empty until 1937.
House completed by contractor Arthur Quinn.
Owner valued the house at $6,000 (federal census).

building_history.site_before: Magner's grocery, saloon and meeting hall, 1880-1890

permit_summary.note: Two of the 11 filings on file carry a nominal valuation and are omitted from the timeline: a street-space permit and an address-verification record.

permits.description: Interior improvements to one unit: expand the kitchen into the existing garage, removing one parking space, a closet and an interior wall.
In-kind replacement of a shower stall, fixtures and finishes.
Dry rot repair at roof level over about 100 sq ft, and replacement of three damaged skylights.
Interior remodel of 440 sq ft at ground floor as habitable space — bedroom, study, bathroom and hall.
Interior remodel at ground level for use as a utility room and storage.
Bathroom remodel; no structural work, existing light fixtures retained.
Replace the two-storey deck, renovate the kitchen, replace the garage door and increase the dwelling from one unit to two, under variance 2005.0615V.
Replace 11 windows at the rear, repaint the upper rear elevation and stain the deck.
Replace kitchen cabinets and the kitchen floor on the second floor.

narrative.lead: One of a pair built side by side on the lower slope of Corbett Avenue.

sources.name: Corbett Heights Neighbors, "June Neighborhood News", Vol. VIII, No. 6 (1 June 2026)
